facts.statement: Seazzadactylus lived during the late Triassic, specifically the Norian stage between 219 and 214 million years ago, in what is now Italy.
facts.quote: Seazzadactylus is a basal pterosaur genus that lived during the late Triassic (Norian stage, about 219-214 million years ago) in the area of present-day Italy.

facts.statement: Amateur paleontologist Umberto Venier discovered the holotype skeleton in 1997 in a boulder in the Seazza brook near Preone in the Dolomites.
facts.quote: In 1997, amateur paleontologist Umberto Venier discovered the skeleton of a pterosaur in a boulder laying in the bed of the Seazza brook, just before it joins the Tagliamento river, near Preone in the Dolomites.

facts.statement: The genus and its type species, Seazzadactylus venieri, were formally named and described by Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, Dalla Vecchia named and described the type species Seazzadactylus venieri.

facts.statement: The generic name Seazzadactylus combines the name of the Seazza brook with the Greek word for 'finger'.
facts.quote: The generic name combines that of the Seazza with the Greek daktylos, 'finger'.

facts.statement: The specific name venieri honors Umberto Venier as the discoverer of the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Venier as discoverer.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MFSN 21545 was found in the Dolomia di Forni Formation dating from the middle to upper Norian.
facts.quote: The holotype, MFSN 21545, was found in a layer of the Dolomia di Forni Formation dating from the middle to upper Norian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton including the skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton with skull and lower jaws.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton lacks the tail and most of the foot bones.
facts.quote: It lacks the tail and most feet bones.

facts.statement: The holotype represents a subadult individual that was not fully grown.
facts.quote: It represents a subadult individual, not fully grown.

facts.statement: The jugal bone features a high front branch that tapers into a sharp, needle-like point.
facts.quote: The jugal bone has a high front branch, tapering to the front and below into a sharp needle-like point.

facts.statement: The shoulder blade is fan-like expanded toward the rear.
facts.quote: The shoulder blade is fan-like expanded to the rear.

facts.statement: The pteroid bone is small and slender, shaped like an exclamation mark.
facts.quote: The pteroid bone is small and slender, formed like an exclamation mark.

facts.statement: Seazzadactylus is classified as a basal pterosaur outside of the Monofenestrata clade.
facts.quote: Seazzadactylus was placed in the Pterosauria in 2019, in a basal position outside of the Monofenestrata.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Seazzadactylus in a clade with Arcticodactylus, Austriadraco, Carniadactylus, Raeticodactylus, and Caviramus.
facts.quote: A cladistic analysis showed it was part of a yet-unnamed clade also containing Arcticodactylus, Austriadraco, Carniadactylus, Raeticodactylus and Caviramus.

facts.statement: The clade containing Seazzadactylus was named Caviramidae in a 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron.
facts.quote: This unnamed clade was eventually named as Caviramidae in a 2020 study by Matthew G. Baron.

facts.statement: In the evolutionary tree, Seazzadactylus is positioned directly above Austriadraco and below Carniadactylus.
facts.quote: In the evolutionary tree Seazzadactylus would be positioned directly above Austriadraco and below Carniadactylus.

facts.statement: Seazzadactylus is classified within the unranked family Eopterosauria.
The time range for Seazzadactylus is recorded as the Norian stage, from 227.3 to 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
